# Junior Web Developer - Full Stack

Remote, USA

Posted Jul 1, 2026

Full-time

Our client is excited to offer a unique opportunity for

futureYou.personTheyWillBecome: A credible, production-ready Junior Full-Stack Developer with 2+ years of professional experience, proven ability to ship features in team environments, and a portfolio of 6+ portfolio projects demonstrating mastery of React, Node.js, and modern web architectures. You will be known for reliability, honest communication, and the ability to take ambiguous requirements and deliver working solutions that users depend on.
futureYou.achievementSummary: Completed 6 portfolio projects (personal + freelance); shipped code in 2-3 client/contract projects with real deadlines and code review processes; earned 3-5 professional references from freelance work; built a GitHub portfolio with 500+ stars across projects; successfully transitioned from bootcamp graduate to hired Junior Full-Stack Developer earning $4,000-5,500/month; demonstrated proficiency in React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and deployment pipelines; established reputation for honest communication and consistent delivery.

phases.goal: Rebuild credibility, correct application materials, and achieve minimum marketable portfolio depth (4 projects) while establishing realistic salary expectations and earning first paid freelance project.
actions: Rewrite all job application materials (resume, LinkedIn, portfolio site) to accurately reflect '2-month post-bootcamp' status; remove all claims of 10 years experience or expertise in 'everything'—be explicit: 'Recently completed intensive coding bootcamp, built working applications, actively seeking first professional role'

Build 3 additional portfolio projects beyond the to-do app: (1) React + Node.js weather app with API integration and PostgreSQL database, (2) Full-stack e-commerce product page with cart functionality and payment integration (Stripe test mode), (3) Real-time chat application using WebSockets demonstrating backend messaging logic

Create a professional portfolio website hosted on Vercel or Netlify showcasing all 4 projects with clear GitHub links, deployed live demos, detailed project write-ups (technical decisions, challenges, learnings), and honest assessment of what you built vs. tutorial-based learning

Secure 1 paid freelance project ($300-800) via Upwork, Fiverr, or local networks (simple website redesign, small feature build, or maintenance work) to gain first professional reference and understand real-world client communication and deadline pressure

Adjust salary expectations: create target ranges by location/role type—research 15-20 junior developer salaries on Glassdoor, Levels.fyi, and local job boards; set realistic first-role target at $3,500-4,500/month; document this research in a personal spreadsheet

Complete 50 coding interview problems on LeetCode (Easy + Medium) focusing on arrays, strings, objects, and problem-solving communication; record yourself explaining solutions aloud to practice verbal communication during technical interviews
skills: Honest self-assessment and accurate professional communication
Full-stack project delivery (React frontend + Node.js backend + database)
API integration and third-party service integration (payments, weather data)
phases.milestone: Portfolio contains 4 complete, deployed projects with clear GitHub repos; first freelance project completed and paid; updated resume/LinkedIn/portfolio site accurately reflect bootcamp-graduate status; salary expectations adjusted to $3,500-4,500/month range documented in writing; 50 LeetCode problems completed with recorded walkthroughs.

phases.goal: Gain 1-2 years of professional experience through contract/freelance work and junior developer role, build deep expertise in React and Node.js, develop team collaboration and code review skills, and establish yourself as a reliable contributor.
actions: Secure a Junior Full-Stack Developer role (contract, part-time, or full-time) at one of the target companies or similar; prioritize roles that explicitly state 'bootcamp graduates welcome' or 'no degree required'; apply to 20-30 of the listed job opportunities across all sources (Scandiweb, AgileEngine, Boomering, Compass, RemoteOtter, etc.) with customized cover letters explaining your bootcamp journey and freelance work

During first professional role, volunteer for code review responsibilities—ask senior developers to review your PRs thoroughly; document 2-3 'code review learnings' each month in a private journal (e.g., 'learned to think about edge cases through PR feedback on date-handling bug'); contribute meaningfully to at least 1 architectural decision or tech discussion

Build 2 additional portfolio projects that showcase production-level thinking: (1) Full-stack SaaS-style app with authentication, user dashboards, data visualization, and deployment pipeline (CI/CD with GitHub Actions or similar), (2) Rebuild one previous project with major improvements—add tests (Jest/React Testing Library), implement error handling, optimize performance, deploy to production with monitoring

Contribute to 1-2 open-source projects (React, Node.js, or JavaScript ecosystem) with 5-10 merged pull requests; focus on bug fixes, documentation, or small feature additions; build reputation visible on GitHub and LinkedIn

Complete 1-2 advanced professional certifications or structured learning: AWS Developer Associate certification (cloud deployment skills highly valued), or Advanced React/Node.js course from Egghead, Frontend Masters, or similar platform focusing on testing, performance, and production patterns

At 12-month mark: update your portfolio with 2 new projects, refresh GitHub README with statistics (contributions, top languages), publish 2-3 technical blog posts on Dev.to or Medium about things you learned (e.g., 'What I Wish I Knew About State Management as a Junior Developer')
skills: Team collaboration and professional code review practices
Testing and quality assurance (Jest, React Testing Library, unit/integration tests)
Deployment and DevOps basics (CI/CD pipelines, environment management, cloud platforms)
Production-level thinking (error handling, performance optimization, monitoring)
Open-source contribution and professional GitHub presence
phases.milestone: Hired as Junior Full-Stack Developer earning $4,500-6,000/month; completed 6+ months employed with 2+ positive professional references; 6 total portfolio projects with 2 built at production-level quality; 5+ merged open-source contributions; AWS Developer Associate certification or equivalent; 2-3 published technical blog posts; GitHub profile shows consistent commits and visible community engagement.

phases.goal: Transition from junior contributor to mid-level/senior engineer; deepen specialization in frontend or full-stack architecture; develop mentorship and leadership capabilities; position for staff-level roles or technical leadership.
actions: Over 2-3 years: deliberately expand into emerging tech relevant to your specialization—if frontend-focused: master Next.js, TypeScript, state management at scale, component libraries; if full-stack-focused: master system design, microservices, database optimization, infrastructure-as-code; pick ONE and go deep (not shallow breadth across everything)

Lead or own 1-2 significant features/projects at your company: define requirements with product, architect the solution, manage implementation across multiple sprints, handle production incidents, and mentor 1-2 junior developers through the process; document your leadership approach in a case study

Build 2-3 'portfolio projects' that demonstrate mid-level thinking: (1) Large-scale project management tool or similar complexity app showing system design decisions, (2) Open-source library or framework contribution that reaches 100+ GitHub stars, (3) Full-stack project incorporating advanced patterns (event-driven architecture, real-time sync, complex caching strategies)

Achieve one of these credentials by year 3: (a) Advanced AWS certification (Solutions Architect or DevOps), (b) TypeScript mastery certification or course completion, (c) System design interview preparation (LeetCode Hard problems, Grokking System Design, or equivalent); demonstrate depth, not breadth

Publish 6-10 technical articles or give 1-2 conference talks/meetup presentations on topics where you have unique perspective (lessons learned from your journey, architectural decisions you've made, mentoring junior developers, etc.)

At 3-year mark: assess readiness for senior developer or staff engineer track—document your impact (features shipped, team/mentees developed, architectural contributions); if staying IC track, target Senior roles paying $7,500-12,000+/month; if targeting leadership, explore tech lead or engineering manager path
skills: Specialization depth in chosen domain (frontend architecture OR full-stack systems design)
Advanced professional practices (monitoring, security, scalability, performance optimization)
Communication and influence—writing, speaking, and shaping technical direction
phases.milestone: Promoted to Senior/Mid-level role or equivalent responsibilities earning $7,500-12,000+/month; led 1-2 major projects from conception to production; mentored 2-3 junior developers with documented impact; published 6+ technical articles or spoke at conferences; maintained 8+ high-quality portfolio projects; established professional reputation in your specialization (recognizable GitHub profile, technical blog following, visible in industry communities); clear trajectory to next career level (staff engineer, tech lead, or engineering manager) defined and communicated.
